Base directory for this skill: /workspaces/oberpierre-skills/skills/slice

# Slice: docs/work/prefix/plan.md merge S2 into S1, so one slice covers the prefix and the unprefixed other notifiers

Turn the decisions in a feature's plan into slices. The argument's first word is the plan only when it is a path or names a plan under `docs/work/`, and the rest is a request, such as `squash S1 and S2`. With no plan named, use the only plan under `docs/work/`, and when there are several or none, ask which plan to slice and stop, even if the request seems to point at one. Read the plan's decision log, and read the code wherever a decision names something that already exists.

You change no code, and you write nothing until the user approves the slices.

Read `.agents/config.yml` if it exists. Its `tracker` key is `markdown` or `github`, and a missing file or key means `markdown`. When the file is not valid YAML, or `tracker` is any other value, report it and stop, proposing nothing. With `github`, run `gh auth status` first, and when `gh` is missing or not logged in, say so and stop, proposing nothing, rather than carrying on with the Markdown plan alone.

## Slices

A slice is one behaviour built end to end and pinned by an acceptance test, small enough to review as a few commits. Cut along behaviours a user or caller can observe, never along layers, so no slice is only a model, only a schema or only wiring. Order them so each slice can be built once the slices it is blocked by are done, and give every decision in the log a slice that carries it out or say why none does.

Each slice is one row of this table:

```
| Slice | Behaviour | Acceptance test | Blocked by | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | <the observable behaviour, in one sentence> | `<test name>`, through <the seam it is tested through> | none | todo | |
```

- **Slice** is the id, `S1`, `S2`… in build order.
- **Acceptance test** names the test and the seam, the public boundary it observes the behaviour through. Its code is written when the slice is built.
- **Blocked by** lists slice ids, or `none`.
- **Status** is `todo`, `done` or `rework`. A new slice is `todo`, and its Note stays empty.

When the plan already has a slices table that lacks one of these columns, has another status or uses an id twice, report each problem and stop, proposing nothing. Fixing it yourself could change what the user approved.

## Proposing

Show the proposed table, with a line under it for anything a reader of the table would ask about, such as why two behaviours share a slice. When the plan has no `**Branch:**` line, suggest a branch name in one of those lines, `<prefix>/<slug>`, with `<slug>` the plan's folder name and `<prefix>` the one of `feature`, `bugfix` and `improvement` that fits what the decisions describe. Then ask the user to approve it or say what to change, and stop. Write nothing in this step.

Most plans raise no questions, and then the table goes out alone. Ask a question only when the table cannot be cut without it: when a different answer would change a slice's behaviour, the seam its test goes through, such as a boundary the code does not have yet, or the order of the slices. Do not ask how a slice is built, such as a signature, where a value is read from, where an error is caught or how an outside service is faked in a test, since that is decided when the slice is built. Do not ask what the log or the code already answers. A needless question costs the user a round.

When a question passes that bar, first call the Skill tool with `grilling`, with those decisions as its argument, and then reply with the table, its lines and the round under them, all in one reply. Once nothing is open, propose the table again with the decisions listed under it.

## Writing

Once the user approves, write the table into the plan under `## Slices`, placed before `## Decision log`. Add each answered question to the decision log as a decision with its reason. Write the approved branch name, as the user left it, on a `` **Branch:** `<name>` `` line under the plan's title, and leave the rest of the plan as it was. Create or switch no branch: the branch is made where the first change is built.

Then challenge the slicing once. Call the Skill tool with `challenge`, with the plan's path followed by `slices` when the table was written for the first time, or by the ids of the slices this run changed, such as `docs/work/sms/plan.md S2 S3`. The decisions were challenged when they were made. If it finds nothing, say so and stop. Otherwise call the Skill tool with `grilling`, with the findings as its argument, and put every finding to the user as one round, each title starting with `Challenge:`. Phrase a defect as "Fix as stated?", and where you disagree with a finding, recommend dismissing it and say why. Record the answers in the decision log, and change the table where an answer changes a slice.

## Rework

When the request names a `done` slice, such as `squash S1 and S2`, first check that its commits are still on the unmerged feature branch: find the commit in the plan's history that set its row to `done`, and see whether it is in the history of the default branch, read from `origin/HEAD`. If it is, say that the slice is merged and a new plan is needed, since rewriting merged commits rewrites shared history, and stop, marking nothing. Otherwise propose the change as a round before touching the plan: call the Skill tool with `grilling`, with the change as its argument, and reply with the round, recommending the shape you think best. Leave `done` slices alone otherwise. Once the user approves, mark each affected slice `rework` with a one-line note of what is to be done, change nothing else of the built slices, and end by naming the `/build` command to run. Run no git command that rewrites history: `build` carries the rework out.

## Mirroring

With `tracker: github`, mirror the slices to GitHub Issues once the challenge's answers are recorded, or at once when the request only asks to mirror an approved table. Read `GITHUB.md` in this skill's folder for the commands, and follow it. The plan stays the source of truth, so never change a slice to match an issue.

Both slices are still `todo`, so this is a plain re-slice and no rework is involved. Here's the proposed table:

| Slice | Behaviour | Acceptance test | Blocked by | Status | Note | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | Every email `EmailNotifier` sends starts with `[shopnotes] `, and other notifiers get the shipping message without the prefix | `test_only_emails_get_the_shop_prefix`, through `on_order_shipped` for order `o1` with a recording notifier beside an `EmailNotifier`, asserting it prints `email via <host> to <customer>: [shopnotes] Order o1 has shipped.` and the recorder got exactly `Order o1 has shipped.` | none | todo | | #2 |

- **Why the two behaviours share a slice:** both follow from one decision, that the prefix goes in `EmailNotifier.send` and nowhere else. One test with an email notifier and a recorder side by side checks both halves through the same call to `on_order_shipped`.
- **Test name:** the two old test names become one, `test_only_emails_get_the_shop_prefix`, because the test now checks both halves.
- **Decision log coverage:** S1 carries out all three decisions. The existing `test_every_notifier_hears_about_a_shipped_order` uses only `Recorder`s, so it keeps passing without changes.
- **GitHub mirror:** S1 keeps issue #2, which I'll update to the merged behaviour. #3 belonged to S2, so I'll close it with a comment pointing to #2.

Approve this, or tell me what to change.

# prefix

**Branch:** `feature/prefix`
**Issue:** #1

Mark every email the shop sends, so customers can filter them.

## Slices

| Slice | Behaviour | Acceptance test | Blocked by | Status | Note | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | The message of every email `EmailNotifier` sends starts with `[shopnotes] ` | `test_email_starts_with_the_shop_prefix`, through `on_order_shipped` for order `o1` with an `EmailNotifier` in its notifiers, asserting it prints `email via <host> to <customer>: [shopnotes] Order o1 has shipped.` | none | todo | | #2 |
| S2 | Notifiers other than `EmailNotifier` get the shipping message without the prefix | `test_other_notifiers_get_no_prefix`, through `on_order_shipped` for order `o1` with a recording notifier beside an `EmailNotifier`, asserting the recorder got exactly `Order o1 has shipped.` | S1 | todo | | #3 |

## Decision log

- `EmailNotifier.send` puts `[shopnotes] ` in front of every message, so `on_order_shipped` and any other notifier stay as they are. Rejected: adding the prefix in `on_order_shipped`, which would also prefix texts.
- The prefix is a fixed string in `EmailNotifier`, not configuration, since the repository serves one shop and nothing else varies it.
- The existing test in `tests/test_shipping.py` keeps passing, since it does not check the email's text.
# Mirroring slices to GitHub Issues

The plan stays the source of truth, and each slice's issue only mirrors its row (ADR 0007). An issue is read by people who never see the plan, which is deleted once the feature is merged, so every issue must make sense on its own: give it a short title in the terms of `GLOSSARY.md`, paraphrasing the row rather than copying it, and open its body with a few plain sentences on what it adds for whoever uses it and why. Run these commands through Bash, one call per command, and read each issue's number from the URL `gh issue create` prints.

## Before the first issue

Run `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner`, and when the repository is not the one the plan belongs to, such as a fork's parent, ask before creating anything.

## First run: the table has no `Issue` column

First create the feature's parent issue, titled and described from the plan's summary, its body ending with a `Feature: <the plan's folder name>` line:

```
gh issue create --title "<title>" --body "<description>

Feature: <slug>"
```

Then create one issue per slice, in the table's order, so that a slice's blockers already have numbers, each a sub-issue of the parent:

```
gh issue create --title "<Behaviour>" --body "<body>" --parent <parent> [--blocked-by <n>,<n>]
```

- The title says what the slice adds, from its Behaviour.
- The body is the description, then three lines: `Acceptance test: <the Acceptance test cell>`, `Feature: <the plan's folder name>`, `Slice: <id>`. A Blocked by entry that is not a slice id goes into the body as one more line, `Blocked by: <entry>`, and gets no link.
- `--blocked-by` lists the issue numbers of the slice ids in Blocked by, and is left out when there are none.

Then close the issue of every `done` slice with `gh issue close <n> --reason completed`.

Add an `Issue` column to the table, after `Note`, holding `#<n>` for each slice, and write a `` **Issue:** #<parent> `` line under the plan's `**Branch:**` line. The parent stays open until `build` closes the plan.

## Later runs: the table has an `Issue` column

Find an issue only by the number in the plan, the slice's `Issue` cell or the `**Issue:**` line, never by searching GitHub.

- A slice this run changed keeps its issue: rewrite its title and body from the new row as on the first run, with `gh issue edit <n> --title "<title>" --body "<body>"`.
- A slice this run added gets an issue as on the first run, a sub-issue of the parent, and its number in the `Issue` column.
- Leave every other issue as it is, even when it differs from its row, since this run did not change that slice.
